answer: Freshness-anchored opal challenge: each registration returns R=Sign_agent(H(opal_t || trellis_root_t || pubkey)); opal_t is a public randomness beacon, trellis_root_t anchors recent actions. Registry rejects duplicate R and accepts only within one beacon epoch. Copying fails because R is epoch- and key-specific. Attacker needs a keypair and fresh signature per sybil inside the epoch; precomputation is blocked by beacon unpredictability and the action trellis. Cost scales with unique signatures and timing pressure.
